small: Keep baby's usual routine on local clock time — a shift this small usually settles on its own
Use blackout blinds and white noise to make the new room feel like home
east: A few days before you leave, try moving bedtime a little earlier each day
On arrival, get outside in morning light to help set the new day
Protect the first nap of each day — skip sightseeing if needed
west: A few days before you leave, try moving bedtime a little later each day

items.title: Wake + feed
items.text: Open curtains straight away — morning light helps set baby's body clock.

items.title: Nap 1 (in stroller or carrier)
items.text: Time this with your first activity. Baby sleeps, you explore.

items.title: Activity window
items.text: Best alert window of the day. Museums, parks, restaurants.

items.title: Lunch + feed
items.text: Baby eats first, then you eat. Try to find a quieter table.

items.title: Nap 2 (back at hotel)
items.text: This is the "protected nap." Do not skip. Use this for your rest too.

items.title: Afternoon activity
items.text: Short outing — shops, a walk, dinner prep area scouting.

items.title: Early dinner
items.text: Aim for 5:30–6pm. Restaurants are quiet. Baby is still cheerful.

items.title: Bedtime routine
items.text: Bath → feed → white noise → dark room. Same routine as home, always.
